DEL-09-06 exists to keep validation, packaging, release, network, key, and instruction-root checks explicit and repeatable for PKG-09 release readiness.

Security checks should demonstrate key material stays outside project truth, renderer/network access is bounded, provider endpoint selection is constrained, and attachment handling does not rely on client metadata.

Principle: runtime code is the security boundary; tests should target runtime behavior such as path containment, permission policy, hooks, redaction, and network controls (PRD Section 4, principles 18-19).

Principle: API keys are convenience state, not project truth; any write of key material to working root, runtime events, logs, git-tracked execution files, SDK transcripts if avoidable, or tool artifacts is a release-blocking failure (K-KEY-1; FR-031, NFR-002).

Principle: renderer and provider network checks should be allowlist-oriented; the shipped posture is loopback plus Anthropic API path, with broader access reserved for governed future scope (K-NET-1; SPEC 16.3).

Principle: Anthropic provider endpoint access and renderer outbound allowlisting are separately enforced surfaces; evidence should not treat one control as proof of the other (PRD FR-032/FR-033; SPEC 16.3; K-NET-1).

Principle: attachment metadata from the browser is advisory only; server-side validation is authoritative for path, type, symlink status, readability, regular-file status, and byte budgets (FR-037; K-ATTACH-1).

Principle: failure behavior is part of the security surface; tests should verify partial attachment failures do not discard executable content and total failure without text returns the typed failure while preserving retry state where the UI is involved (FR-040; SPEC 16.1).
Endpoint tests must be strict about credentials and ports: https://api.anthropic.com with credentials or a non-empty non-443 port is not equivalent to the accepted base URL.
Prefer negative tests for sensitive paths: denied network URL, unsupported extension, symlink, directory, over-budget file, unreadable file, and redaction of realistic key-shaped strings.
Do not treat allowedTools or SDK permissions alone as sufficient; Chirality-owned overlays remain required for professional safety.
Exact implementation file paths are TBD until confirmed by the relevant feature deliverables.
Trade-off: unit tests isolate policy logic while integration tests prove route/Electron behavior; use both where the surface crosses Electron, SDK provider, or route boundaries.

Trade-off: broad redaction fixture scanning risks false positives and narrow checks risk missing variants; include representative key variants and verify both redaction and non-secret metadata retention.
Trade-off: UI retry behavior may sit outside the resolver; keep resolver validation separate from route/UI retry preservation to localize failures.
Trade-off: provider execution requires Anthropic access while renderer traffic must stay constrained; test renderer and Node/SDK provider policy as separate surfaces with a shared policy vocabulary.
Example: base URL https://api.anthropic.com is accepted when credentials are absent and port is empty or 443 (FR-032).
Example: a base URL with embedded credentials is rejected (FR-032).
Example: a renderer request to a non-loopback, non-Anthropic URL is cancelled and logged without secrets (FR-033).
Example: an attachment path pointing to a symlink is rejected before provider execution (SPEC 16.1; NFR-004).
Example: when one attachment fails but text or another valid attachment remains, the turn may proceed with a warning (SPEC 16.1).
Example: when all attachments fail and text is empty, the request fails with ATTACHMENT_FAILURE (SPEC 16.1).
